title_en: Israel’s war on homes: From Hebron to Gaza and southern Lebanon
title_zh: 以色列对家园的战争：从希伯伦到加沙和黎巴嫩南部
summary: From Hebron to Gaza to southern Lebanon, Israel is tearing down homes, and, with them, families' hopes of return.
summary_zh: 从希伯伦到加沙，再到黎巴嫩南部，以色列正在拆除房屋，并摧毁了家庭返回的希望。
body_en: Israel’s war on homes: From Hebron to Gaza and southern Lebanon | Israel-Palestine conflict | Al Jazeera
From Hebron to Gaza to southern Lebanon, Israel is tearing down homes, and with them, families' hopes of return.

“Around 12:30 at night, the Israeli army vehicles were at al-Jalda Square,” one Hebron resident told Al Jazeera. “They told us to leave our homes. We asked until when, and they said until further notice. We left with the clothes on our backs.”

Hours earlier on October 23, two Israeli soldiers had been killed by armed Palestinian men at a checkpoint near the city. Hebron, the occupied West Bank’s largest city, has been under Israeli siege ever since, with restrictions extending across a governorate of about 800,000 Palestinians.
A black X now marks the homes from which families have been forcibly expelled. Soldiers have moved into others, turning them into military outposts.

In just over a week, nearly 5,000 Palestinians have been displaced, according to UNRWA, the United Nations agency for Palestinian refugees, which called the measures collective punishment in violation of international law.

The current operation builds on years of demolitions. From 2009 up until the siege began on October 23, Israeli forces demolished 2,491 buildings and displaced 3,534 Palestinians in the Hebron governorate, according to the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). Across Area C and occupied East Jerusalem, the monthly average of demolitions since 2024 has been at least double that of the preceding 15 years.
Many demolitions are linked to Israel’s restrictive permit system. Palestinians struggle to obtain Israeli-issued building permits, leaving structures built without them vulnerable to demolition.

In Masafer Yatta, a cluster of 13 communities in the South Hebron Hills, Israeli authorities have demolished about 400 structures in 15 years, displacing 969 Palestinians. Nearly half were demolished since January 2025.

UNRWA’s West Bank director, Roland Friedrich, said the scenes in Hebron carry “alarming echoes” of the mass displacement in the northern occupied West Bank in early 2025, when Israeli military operations emptied the Jenin, Tulkarem and Nur Shams refugee camps.

More than 34,000 Palestinian refugees from the Jenin, Tulkarem and Nur Shams camps remain displaced, according to UNRWA, more than a year after Israel’s “Iron Wall” operation began in January 2025. The operation destroyed more than half of the camps’ residential buildings.

OCHA’s demolition records capture only a fraction of that destruction. Between 2009 and October 2026, the agency recorded 1,399 buildings demolished in the Jenin and Tulkarem governorates, displacing 4,139 people. Those records mainly track demolitions carried out for lack of permits or as punishment, not buildings destroyed during military raids.

An investigation by the research group Forensic Architecture found evidence of deliberate, systematic destruction. Researchers verified more than 200 incidents involving the destruction of buildings and streets across four refugee camps, using armoured bulldozers, controlled demolitions and air attacks. They found that roads were widened through homes and gardens to create routes for military vehicles. The group concluded that Israel was applying tactics in the occupied West Bank similar to those it had used in Gaza.
In February 2025, Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said Tulkarem and Jenin would come to resemble Jabalia and Shujayea, two of Gaza’s most devastated areas.

The raids have not stopped. Last week, Israeli forces detained four Palestinians in Tulkarem, and in the village of Burin, south of Nablus, troops converted several homes into military barracks, as they have in Hebron.

Near Jenin, the army has ordered the residents of an entire village to leave permanently. “I have sheep and cows. Our entire lives are tied to this land,” said farmer Jabri Yahya. “Last year they uprooted our olive trees, and this year they want to force us to leave. We don’t know where to go.”

In Gaza, the destruction is on a far larger scale. By June 16, 2026, an estimated 201,290 structures had been damaged or destroyed, about 82 percent of all structures in the Strip, according to the UN Satellite Centre (UNOSAT).
Many families now shelter in tents , makeshift structures or damaged buildings, often without reliable water or sanitation.

Another winter brings new risks . Mohammed al-Jamal, 60, has been displaced several times since he fled his home in Gaza City’s Shujayea neighbourhood. He now shares a worn-out tent on the beach with about 30 members of his extended family, patching it before every storm because they cannot afford a new tarpaulin. “We are living in the street, not in houses that protect us,” he said.

Across the Strip, the neighbourhoods families fled have been reduced to rubble. Google Maps satellite imagery updated in September shows the scale of the destruction across the besieged Gaza Strip, more than three years into Israel’s genocidal war .
body_zh: 以色列对家园的战争：从希伯伦到加沙和黎巴嫩南部|以色列-巴勒斯坦冲突|半岛电视台
从希伯伦到加沙再到黎巴嫩南部，以色列正在拆毁房屋，并摧毁了家庭返回的希望。
“晚上 12 点 30 分左右，以色列军车停在贾尔达广场，”一名希伯伦居民告诉半岛电视台。 “他们让我们离开家。我们问到什么时候，他们说直到另行通知。我们就背着衣服离开了。”
10 月 23 日几个小时前，两名以色列士兵在该市附近的一个检查站被巴勒斯坦武装人员杀害。被占领的约旦河西岸最大城市希伯伦此后一直处于以色列的围困之下，限制范围遍及约 80 万巴勒斯坦人的省份。
现在，一个黑色的“X”标记了那些被强行驱逐的家庭。士兵们已经转移到其他地方，把它们变成军事前哨。
联合国巴勒斯坦难民机构近东救济工程处表示，在短短一周多的时间里，就有近 5000 名巴勒斯坦人流离失所，该机构称这些集体惩罚措施违反了国际法。
目前的运作是建立在多年拆除的基础上的。据人道主义事务协调办公室 (OCHA) 称，从 2009 年到 10 月 23 日围困开始，以色列军队在希伯伦省拆除了 2,491 座建筑物，并导致 3,534 名巴勒斯坦人流离失所。在 C 区和被占领的东耶路撒冷，自 2024 年以来的月平均拆除数量至少是前 15 年的两倍。
许多拆除活动都与以色列的限制性许可证制度有关。巴勒斯坦人很难获得以色列颁发的建筑许可证，因此没有许可证而建造的建筑很容易被拆除。
在南希伯伦山由 13 个社区组成的 Masafer Yatta，以色列当局在 15 年内拆除了约 400 栋建筑，导致 969 名巴勒斯坦人流离失所。自 2025 年 1 月以来，近一半被拆除。
近东救济工程处西岸主任罗兰·弗里德里希表示，希伯伦的场景与 2025 年初被占领的西岸北部发生的大规模流离失所现象“令人震惊”，当时以色列的军事行动清空了杰宁、图勒卡里姆和努尔沙姆斯难民营。
据近东救济工程处称，距离以色列于 2025 年 1 月开始实施“铁墙”行动一年多后，来自杰宁、图勒卡里姆和努尔沙姆斯难民营的超过 34,000 名巴勒斯坦难民仍然流离失所。该行动摧毁了难民营一半以上的住宅建筑。
人道协调厅的拆除记录仅记录了破坏的一小部分。 2009年至2026年10月期间，该机构记录称，杰宁省和图勒凯尔姆省有1,399座建筑物被拆除，导致4,139人流离失所。这些记录主要追踪因缺乏许可证或作为惩罚而进行的拆除，而不是军事袭击期间被毁坏的建筑物。
法医建筑研究小组的一项调查发现了蓄意、系统性破坏的证据。研究人员核实了 200 多起涉及四个难民营的建筑物和街道被毁坏的事件，其中包括使用装甲推土机、控制性拆除和空袭。他们发现穿过房屋和花园的道路被拓宽，为军用车辆开辟了路线。该组织得出的结论是，以色列在被占领的约旦河西岸采用了与加沙类似的战术。
2025 年 2 月，以色列财政部长贝扎雷尔·斯莫特里奇表示，图勒凯尔姆和杰宁将变得类似于加沙受灾最严重的两个地区贾巴利亚和舒贾耶。
袭击并未停止。上周，以色列军队在图勒凯尔姆拘留了四名巴勒斯坦人，在纳布卢斯以南的布林村，以色列军队将几处房屋改造成军营，就像在希伯伦一样。
在杰宁附近，军队已命令整个村庄的居民永久离开。 “我养了羊和牛。我们的一生都与这片土地息息相关，”农民贾布里·叶海亚 (Jabri Yahya) 说。 “去年他们把我们的橄榄树连根拔起，今年他们想强迫我们离开。我们不知道该去哪里。”
在加沙，破坏的规模要大得多。根据联合国卫星中心 (UNOSAT) 的数据，截至 2026 年 6 月 16 日，估计有 201,290 座建筑物遭到损坏或摧毁，约占拉斯维加斯大道所有建筑物的 82%。
许多家庭现在躲在帐篷、临时建筑或受损的建筑物中，往往没有可靠的水或卫生设施。
又一个冬天带来了新的风险。 60 岁的穆罕默德·贾马尔 (Mohammed al-Jamal) 自从逃离加沙市舒贾耶 (Shujayea) 社区的家以来，已多次流离失所。现在，他与大约 30 名大家庭成员在海滩上共用一个破旧的帐篷，每次暴风雨前都会修补它，因为他们买不起新的防水布。 “我们住在街上，而不是住在保护我们的房子里，”他说。
拉斯维加斯大道对面，家庭逃离的社区已化为废墟。九月更新的谷歌地图卫星图像显示了以色列种族灭绝战争三年多以来，被围困的加沙地带的破坏规模。

title_en: Shops looted as German cost of living protests turn violent
title_zh: 德国生活成本抗议演变成暴力，商店被洗劫
summary: The protests in cities across Germany - including Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt - came on the same day hundreds of thousands also protested in France.
summary_zh: 法兰克福警方表示，市中心发生了“暴力骚乱”，柏林、汉堡和科隆也有报道称发生骚乱。
body_en: Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday as clashes erupted in German cities over the cost of living.

Besides Frankfurt - Germany's financial hub - there were incidents of violence in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg, with police saying they used water cannon to disperse protesters targeting emergency workers with fireworks, stones and bottles.

Thousands joined largely peaceful demonstrations earlier in the day. They were organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt - meaning "Gen Z takes charge" - to protest against underfunding in schools, the high cost of living, public spending cuts and military service.
The unrest in Germany follows similar youth-led mass protests in France, where more than 320,000 people also demonstrated on Saturday.
As night fell, demonstrations turned violent.
A large section of Frankfurt's main shopping street was closed off by police. A police spokesperson said many arrests were made in the city.

Authorities in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, roughly half of what the organisers had estimated on their website. German media say tens of thousands protested in German cities on Saturday.
Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich said the demonstrations were "to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion".
She said: "What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service and we are in favour of a fairer distribution of the burden."
Europe's youth is on the march - but does anything actually unite them?

On Saturday night Frankfurt police said "violent riots" were occurring in the city centre and that special police units had been deployed. The windows of several shops had been smashed and molotov cocktails were thrown at emergency services, police said.

Officials said the windows of a gun shop were smashed and that they had seized two weapons after arresting a suspect. People also broke into other shops, stealing trainers and other items, local media reported.

Roman Poseck, interior minister of Hesse state, of which Frankfurt is the biggest city, said that "around 100 clearly identified left-wing extremists" had infiltrated the protest in the city. He added that it was "shameful" how the protests had ended.

Poseck said: "We all have those images from France in our minds - looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers... France must not be held up as a model in this regard."
Police said the situation calmed down overnight into Sunday in the city.
Similar instances took place in other German cities, following earlier largely peaceful demonstrations.
In Cologne, police said officers were attacked near the main train station, with bottles thrown and a bicycle launched.

Cologne's police chief Johannes Hermanns said it was "deeply saddening that young people who wanted to peacefully demonstrate for their future were infiltrated today by extremists who had nothing but violence in mind".
A smaller demonstration in the evening in Berlin - following larger protests in the day - resulted in 27 police officers being injured, and up to 56 people temporarily detained, Berlin police said.
In Hamburg, people dressed in black set off fireworks and set barricades on fire, with public broadcaster NDR reporting that 120 people were arrested.
body_zh: 周六晚间，随着德国各城市因生活成本问题爆发冲突，暴乱者抢劫了法兰克福市中心的商店。
除了德国金融中心法兰克福外，柏林、科隆和汉堡也发生了暴力事件，警方表示，他们使用高压水枪驱散抗议者，这些抗议者向急救人员投掷烟花、石块和瓶子。
当天早些时候，数千人参加了基本上和平的示威活动。这些活动是由运动团体 Gen Z regelt（意思是“Z 世代负责”）组织的，目的是抗议学校资金不足、生活成本高昂、公共开支削减和兵役。
德国发生骚乱之前，法国也发生了类似的青年领导的大规模抗议活动，周六也有超过 32 万人示威。
夜幕降临，示威活动变得暴力。
法兰克福主要购物街的一大片区域被警方封锁。警方发言人表示，该市逮捕了许多人。
法兰克福、慕尼黑和柏林当局报告称抗议者人数多达 18,000 人，大约是组织者在其网站上估计人数的一半。
Gen Z regelt 发言人莉娜·弗里德里希 (Lina Friedrich) 表示，示威活动是“为了和平与自由而战，而不是为了战争和胁迫”。
她说：“对我们来说最重要的是更好地支持卫生和教育系统。我们反对义务兵役制，我们赞成更公平地分配负担。”
欧洲的年轻人正在前进——但有什么东西能够真正将他们团结起来呢？
周六晚上，法兰克福警方表示市中心发生“暴力骚乱”，并已部署特警部队。警方称，几家商店的窗户被砸碎，并向紧急服务部门投掷燃烧弹。
官员们表示，一家枪店的窗户被砸碎，他们在逮捕一名嫌疑人后缴获了两把武器。据当地媒体报道，人们还闯入其他商店，偷走运动鞋和其他物品。
黑森州（法兰克福是黑森州最大的城市）内政部长罗曼·波塞克（Roman Poseck）表示，“大约 100 名明确身份的左翼极端分子”已渗透到该市的抗议活动中。他补充说，抗议活动的结束方式是“可耻的”。
波塞克说：“我们脑海中都有来自法国的那些画面——抢劫、焚烧房屋、焚烧警车、袭击警察……法国在这方面绝不能成为榜样。”
警方表示，该市的局势到周日夜间已经平静下来。
继早些时候基本和平的示威活动之后，类似的情况在德国其他城市也发生了。
在科隆，警方表示，警察在火车总站附近遭到袭击，有人投掷瓶子，还扔了一辆自行车。
科隆警察局长约翰内斯·赫尔曼斯表示，“令人深感悲痛的是，那些想要为自己的未来和平示威的年轻人今天却被只想着暴力的极端分子渗透”。
柏林警方表示，继当天规模较大的抗议活动之后，柏林晚上举行了一场规模较小的示威活动，导致 27 名警察受伤，多达 56 人被暂时拘留。
在汉堡，黑衣人燃放烟花并纵火路障，公共广播公司 NDR 报道称，有 120 人被捕。

title_en: Gaza doctors struggle with bereavement, overwork, trauma amid genocidal war
title_zh: 加沙医生在种族灭绝战争中与丧亲之痛、过度劳累和创伤作斗争
summary: Doctors and nurses struggle to cope with the horrors they endured during the height of the Gaza war.
summary_zh: 医生和护士努力应对加沙战争最激烈时期所遭受的恐怖。
body_en: Share Gaza doctors struggle with bereavement, overwork, trauma amid genocidal war on social media
Deir el-Balah, Gaza – Manar Fayyad, 29, an anaesthesiologist at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital , has suffered severe psychological trauma since the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023.
The turning point came when he discovered that a man lying before him in the operating room was his own brother Shadi, who was killed in an Israeli air strike on December 27, 2023.

He recalled the moment he was summoned into the operating room to administer anaesthesia to a critically injured man before emergency surgery.

“He died before I could reach him,” he said. “When I arrived in the operating room, I recognised the man’s clothes. I had a strange feeling, so I approached him and uncovered his face. To my shock, he was my brother Shadi, who was 34.”
Since then, the hospital has become inseparable from the traumatic memory, and he has been unable to continue to work, ultimately bringing his professional career to a premature end.

He continues to struggle with the psychological effects of the experience, trying to cope with it on his own without professional help. He has withdrawn from social life and avoids people and noise as he searches for peace since his brother died.

Sitting by the sea and writing offers him some solace, helping him express his pain and process what has happened. Yet he remains preoccupied with the idea of leaving Gaza, hoping that distance might free him from the reminders of that day.
Having lost his brother, his profession and much of his social life, Fayyad now faces a different battle: one against trauma that he is trying to confront alone.

Khaled Raafat, 29, a nurse in the emergency department at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital, stepped away from work for an extended period after losing his wife, children, mother and several siblings in an Israeli air strike on his family home on October 18, 2023. He was at the hospital at the time, trying to save their lives of others injured that day.

“Learning that I had lost my family marked a painful turning point in my life,” Khaled told Al Jazeera. “I could no longer do my job in the same way. The hospital, once associated in my mind with my humanitarian duty, became a reminder of personal pain that was beyond what I could bear. It deeply affected my ability to continue my professional and social life.”
Raafat said he eventually decided to rebuild his life.

“I realised that life could not stop at the tragedy and that I had to find a way to carry on. I decided to work towards my psychological recovery, got married and started a new family in an attempt to regain stability and hope,” he said. “I then returned to work at the hospital.”
At least 1,700 medical personnel have been killed in Israeli attacks during the war while 83 healthcare workers remain in Israeli detention, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office.

These figures do not reveal the deep psychological burden borne by medical workers who have lost family, friends and colleagues and witnessed horrific injuries and death on a daily basis. They have also faced continued displacement, relentless pressure and have been overworked for years.

A study found that 41 percent reported losing family members and 46 percent had experienced both personal bereavement and displacement from their workplaces, according to a report on the strain on medical workers in Gaza published in the Public Library of Science .

At least 78 percent of healthcare workers in Gaza lacked access to mental health services, showing the gap between the trauma healthcare workers endure and their access to psychological care. It has meant that Gaza’s health system is struggling to retain its remaining staff and prevent them from leaving the medical field.
body_zh: 加沙医生在社交媒体上的种族灭绝战争中与丧亲之痛、过度劳累和创伤作斗争
加沙代尔巴拉赫——29 岁的马纳尔·法耶兹 (Manar Fayyad) 是阿克萨烈士医院的麻醉师，自 2023 年 10 月以色列对加沙的种族灭绝战争爆发以来，他遭受了严重的心理创伤。
当他发现手术室里躺在他面前的一个人是他自己的兄弟沙迪时，转折点出现了，沙迪在 2023 年 12 月 27 日的以色列空袭中丧生。

他回忆起他被叫进手术室，在紧急手术前为一名重伤男子进行麻醉的那一刻。
“我还没来得及找到他，他就死了，”他说。 “当我到达手术室时，我认出了那个人的衣服。我有一种奇怪的感觉，所以我走近他，揭开了他的脸。令我震惊的是，他是我34岁的弟弟沙迪。”
从此，医院与创伤记忆密不可分，他也无法继续工作，最终导致他的职业生涯提前结束。
他继续与这次经历的心理影响作斗争，试图在没有专业帮助的情况下独自应对。自从他哥哥去世后，他退出了社交生活，避开人群和噪音，寻求平静。
坐在海边写作给了他一些安慰，帮助他表达痛苦并处理所发生的事情。然而，他仍然全神贯注于离开加沙的想法，希望这种距离能让他摆脱那天的回忆。
失去了兄弟、职业和大部分社交生活后，法耶兹现在面临着一场不同的战斗：一场他试图独自面对的创伤的战斗。
29 岁的哈立德·拉法特 (Khaled Raafat) 是阿克萨烈士医院急诊科的一名护士，2023 年 10 月 18 日，以色列空袭他的家，他失去了妻子、孩子、母亲和几个兄弟姐妹，之后他长时间没有工作。当时他正在医院，试图挽救当天受伤的其他人的生命。
哈立德告诉半岛电视台：“得知我失去了家人，这标志着我人生中一个痛苦的转折点。” “我不能再以同样的方式完成我的工作。曾经在我心目中，医院与我的人道主义义务联系在一起，但它却让我想起了超出我所能承受的个人痛苦。它深深地影响了我继续我的职业和社交生活的能力。”
拉法特说，他最终决定重建自己的生活。
“我意识到生活不能因悲剧而停止，我必须找到继续下去的方法。我决定努力恢复心理，结婚并组建新家庭，试图重新获得稳定和希望，”他说。 “然后我又回到医院工作。”
据加沙政府媒体办公室称，战争期间至少有 1,700 名医务人员在以色列的袭击中丧生，而 83 名医护人员仍被以色列拘留。
这些数字并没有揭示那些失去家人、朋友和同事、每天目睹可怕的伤害和死亡的医务人员所承受的深层心理负担。他们还面临着持续的流离失所、无情的压力以及多年来的过度劳累。
根据公共科学图书馆发表的关于加沙医务人员压力的报告，一项研究发现，41% 的人表示失去了家人，46% 的人经历了个人丧亲和离开工作场所。
加沙至少 78% 的医护人员无法获得心理健康服务，这表明医护人员所承受的创伤与他们获得心理护理的机会之间存在差距。这意味着加沙的卫生系统正在努力留住剩余的工作人员，并阻止他们离开医疗领域。

title_en: Ukrainian evacuees reunite with family after years trapped in Russia-occupied city
title_zh: 被困俄罗斯占领城市多年的乌克兰撤离人员与家人团聚
summary: Oleshky residents had been without food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.
summary_zh: 奥列什基居民一直没有食物、水和电，许多人靠烹饪花园里的杂草来生存。
body_en: By Dan Johnson , Ukraine correspondent , Reporting from Chernihiv and Jacob Phillips
There were raw emotional scenes as people evacuated from the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky crossed from Belarus into the Ukrainian region of Chernihiv.
Families cried as they reunited with relatives they had not seen for years, with two sisters running and crying out as they embraced their father.

Some elderly residents were so weak they were carried on stretchers. They had been trapped in the frontline city without food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky thanked US First Lady Melania Trump for her efforts in brokering a local ceasefire that paved the way for their evacuation on Friday.
Upon their arrival, Dasha and Anya Palii sprinted across the tarmac screaming towards the bus carrying their father Mykhailo.
Their cries and their tears captured the sheer relief of three years of desperate worry, fearing they would never see him again.
Their mother Zhanna clasped Mykhailo's face and stroked his forehead again and again, as if checking he was the same man she had left behind. He promised her, finally, they will now get married.

Tetiana and Volodymyr, an older couple carrying their cat, told the BBC they no longer have a home, after it was burned down in the first year of the war. They have been living in the abandoned house of a neighbour.
They said they instantly took the decision to leave but feared their journey could be disrupted. Now they have to work out where to go next and how to rebuild their lives.

Ukrainian military positions lie just 5km (3.1 miles) from Oleshky, but evacuees first had to travel through Russian-occupied territory to southern Russia, where they flew to Belarus, before finally being driven across Ukraine's northern border on Saturday.
The oldest evacuee was 94 years old, while the youngest was one, according to Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman.

Zelensky said in a post on X that "all of them will receive the assistance they need. It is important that government agencies and all the regional and local authorities involved work effectively and help our people adapt."

Many people bear the scars: the convoy includes as many ambulances as coaches. The impact of years caught between the frontlines is written on the weary faces of many of Oleshky's residents, some hobbling on crutches, others needing wheelchairs.
They have a lot to come to terms with, not least having left the place they call home.

A humanitarian ceasefire took effect across the frontline region of Kherson on Tuesday, providing the first few days of peace in the area in four years, following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Before the war, Oleshky was home to 24,000 people.

Conditions had become so desperate in the city that not only was getting supplies into the city extremely difficult, but escape was highly dangerous because the routes out had been mined and subject to drone attack.
Bridges across the nearby River Dnipro have been destroyed and sources say the riverbank has been mined and is dangerous.
One resident who fled the city three weeks earlier told the BBC he had walked through 24km (15 miles) of minefields to get to safety.
The ceasefire allowed the road out of the city to be cleared of mines and humanitarian aid to be delivered.
body_zh: 丹·约翰逊，乌克兰记者，切尔尼戈夫和雅各布·菲利普斯报道
当人们从被俄罗斯占领的奥列什基市撤离，从白俄罗斯越境进入乌克兰切尔尼戈夫地区时，出现了令人激动的场景。
当家人与多年未见的亲戚团聚时，他们哭了，两个姐妹一边跑一边哭着拥抱父亲。
一些老人身体虚弱，只能用担架抬走。他们被困在前线城市，没有食物、水和电，许多人靠烹饪花园里的杂草来生存。
乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基感谢美国第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普为促成当地停火所做的努力，为周五的撤离铺平了道路。
抵达后，达莎和安雅·帕利冲过停机坪，尖叫着冲向载着父亲米凯洛的巴士。
他们的哭声和泪水让三年来的绝望忧虑得到了彻底的缓解，担心他们再也见不到他了。
他们的母亲詹娜捧着米凯洛的脸，一次又一次地抚摸他的额头，仿佛要确认他还是她留下的那个人。他最终向她保证，他们现在就要结婚。
Tetiana 和 Volodymyr 是一对带着猫的老夫妇，他们告诉 BBC，自从战争第一年被烧毁后，他们就不再有家了。他们一直住在邻居废弃的房子里。
他们说，他们立即决定离开，但担心他们的旅程可能会受到干扰。现在他们必须弄清楚下一步该去哪里以及如何重建他们的生活。
乌克兰军事阵地距离奥列什基仅 5 公里（3.1 英里），但撤离人员首先必须穿过俄罗斯占领的领土前往俄罗斯南部，然后飞往白俄罗斯，最后于周六被驱车穿过乌克兰北部边境。
乌克兰人权监察员德米特罗·鲁比涅茨 (Dmytro Lubinets) 表示，撤离者中年龄最大的是 94 岁，最年轻的只有 1 岁。
泽连斯基在 X 上发帖称，“他们所有人都将获得所需的援助。重要的是，政府机构以及所有相关地区和地方当局必须有效工作并帮助我们的人民适应。”
许多人都留下了伤疤：车队中的救护车和教练一样多。奥列什基的许多居民疲惫的脸上都写满了多年来在前线的影响，有些人拄着拐杖一瘸一拐，另一些人则需要轮椅。
他们有很多事情要面对，尤其是离开了他们称之为家的地方。
周二，人道主义停火在赫尔松前线地区生效，这是该地区自 2022 年 2 月俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰以来四年来首次实现和平。战前，奥列什基居住着 24,000 人。
这座城市的情况已经变得非常严峻，不仅将物资运送到城市极其困难，而且逃跑也非常危险，因为出去的路线布满了地雷，并且容易受到无人机的袭击。
附近第聂伯河上的桥梁已被摧毁，消息人士称河岸已布有地雷，十分危险。
一名三周前逃离该市的居民告诉 BBC，他穿过 24 公里（15 英里）的雷区才到达安全地带。
停火使得出城道路上的地雷得以清除，人道主义援助得以运送。

title_en: India's opposition holds mega rally seeking election chief's resignation
title_zh: 印度反对派将举行大型集会寻求选举主席辞职
summary: It comes amid growing protests over a voter roll revision exercise feared to leave 130 million voters off rolls.
summary_zh: 此举正值选民名册修改活动引发越来越多的抗议，担心选民名册修改将导致 1.3 亿选民被剔除。
body_en: Tens of thousands of people have gathered in Delhi for a major opposition rally demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner.

The rally, organised by the opposition INDIA bloc and led by Rahul Gandhi's Congress party, is taking place at Ramlila Maidan, a large ground in central Delhi known for hosting cultural events and political protests.

Visuals showed Gandhi in an open-top jeep alongside other opposition leaders heading towards the venue. The Gen Z-led pressure group Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has also pledged support, though its leaders have yet to be seen.
Security has been tightened, with thousands of police and paramilitary personnel deployed near the grounds.
Sunday's event is the latest show of opposition anger over a voter-list revision exercise that has removed 130 million names from draft electoral rolls in India.
The Election Commission of India (ECI) says the exercise is aimed at updating the voters' list by purging names of people who have died or moved away from their registered addresses.

But opposition parties allege that the exercise - known as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) - could benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) by removing eligible voters from the rolls. They accuse the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the BJP of "vote chori (theft)". Both the BJP and the ECI have denied the allegations.

The controversy intensified in September when The Indian Express newspaper in its investigation , external reported that the CEC, Gyanesh Kumar, made key decisions related to the exercise without the agreement of the two other election commissioners, who had raised objections on more than a dozen occasions.
The Election Commission said differences of opinion were normal in any institution and did not affect its functioning.
But concerns over the revision process have continued, with the opposition parties, the CJP and student groups organising a number of protests in Delhi and other Indian cities.

On Saturday, leaders of the INDIA bloc staged a symbolic impeachment of Kumar at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence in Delhi. The INDIA bloc - short for Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance - is a group of opposition parties formed in 2023 to take on the governing BJP-led National Democratic Alliance.

The mock parliamentary session, presided over by former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar, saw leaders accuse the election chief of "conspiring to steal elections" and deliberately removing 130 million voters from electoral rolls.

Kharge, who is also the leader of the opposition in parliament's upper house, moved a symbolic motion seeking Kumar's removal, accusing him of undermining the electoral process and committing an act of "treason against the nation and the Constitution of India".
Several people whose names had been removed from electoral rolls during the revision exercise also attended the event.
The proceedings were purely symbolic and had no legal standing. Under Indian law, the chief election commissioner can only be removed through a formal parliamentary process.

Prime Minister Modi has not directly commented on the mock impeachment proceedings. However, speaking at a public rally on Friday, he said that "some people" wanted to create chaos across the country so that he could be defamed.
Later on Saturday, while addressing a separate rally, he also accused opposition parties of "abandoning their duty" and "tearing apart the dignity and boundaries of the constitution".

Last month, Congress MP and leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi led tens of thousands of protesters in a march from Connaught Place in central Delhi to the Supreme Court, seeking the CEC's resignation.
"The march was just the trailer," a party leader told the BBC, adding that "Sunday's rally will be several times bigger than that".

Ahead of the rally, Gandhi said their protest was against "the demolition of Indian democracy", adding that "all the opposition parties and everybody who wants to come, political or non-political, is welcome".
body_zh: 数万人聚集在德里举行大型反对派集会，要求印度首席选举专员辞职。
这次集会由反对派印度集团组织，由拉胡尔·甘地领导的国大党领导，在拉姆利拉迈丹举行，这是德里市中心的一大片场地，以举办文化活动和政治抗议活动而闻名。
视频显示甘地乘坐一辆敞篷吉普车与其他反对派领导人一起前往会场。 Z 世代领导的压力组织蟑螂简塔党 (CJP) 也承诺提供支持，但其领导人尚未露面。
安全措施已经加强，数千名警察和准军事人员部署在场地附近。
周日的活动是反对派对选民名单修改行动感到愤怒的最新表现，此次修改行动已从印度的选民名单中删除了 1.3 亿人的名字。
印度选举委员会（ECI）表示，此次活动的目的是通过删除已死亡或搬离登记地址的人的姓名来更新选民名单。
但反对党声称，这项被称为“特别强化修订”（SIR）的活动可能会通过将符合资格的选民从名册中剔除而使总理纳伦德拉·莫迪领导的印度人民党（BJP）受益。他们指责首席选举专员（CEC）和印度人民党“盗窃选票”。印度人民党和 ECI 均否认了这些指控。
9月，《印度快报》在调查中对外报道称，中央选举委员会Gyanesh Kumar在未征得其他两名选举委员同意的情况下做出了与此次演习相关的关键决定，而这两名选举委员已多次提出反对意见，争议进一步加剧。
选举委员会表示，意见分歧在任何机构都是正常现象，不会影响其运作。
但对修订进程的担忧仍在继续，反对党、印度人民党和学生团体在德里和其他印度城市组织了多次抗议活动。
周六，印度集团领导人在国大党主席马利卡琼·哈格位于德里的官邸对库马尔进行了象征性弹劾。印度集团是印度国家发展包容性联盟的缩写，是一个由反对党组成的团体，成立于 2023 年，旨在对抗印度人民党领导的执政的全国民主联盟。
模拟议会会议由前人民院议长梅拉·库马尔主持，领导人指责选举负责人“密谋窃取选举”并故意将 1.3 亿选民从选民名单中剔除。
哈格也是议会上院反对党领袖，他提出了一项象征性动议，要求库马尔下台，指责他破坏选举进程，并犯下“背叛国家和印度宪法”的行为。
一些在修改过程中名字被从选民名册中删除的人也参加了这次活动。
该诉讼纯粹是象征性的，没有法律地位。根据印度法律，首席选举专员只能通过正式的议会程序被罢免。
莫迪总理尚未直接对模拟弹劾程序发表评论。然而，他在周五的一次公开集会上发表讲话时表示，“一些人”想要在全国制造混乱，以便诽谤他。
周六晚些时候，他在另一场集会上发表讲话时，还指责反对党“放弃职责”并“撕裂宪法的尊严和界限”。
上个月，国大党议员兼反对党领袖拉胡尔·甘地率领数万名抗议者从德里市中心的康诺特广场游行至最高法院，要求中央选举委员会辞职。
一位政党领导人告诉英国广播公司：“游行只是预告片”，并补充说“周日的集会规模将是其数倍”。
集会前，甘地表示，他们的抗议是反对“摧毁印度民主”，并补充说“欢迎所有反对党和所有愿意参加的人，无论是政治的还是非政治的”。

body_en: Binance says 90% of losses from $6.3bn hack covered as FBI says North Korea behind attack | Binance
Binance says 90% of losses from $6.3bn hack covered as FBI says North Korea behind attack
Cryptocurrency exchange says withdrawals starting to resume on Sunday as FBI blames North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says it has replaced 90% of the ⁠amount stolen after a record $6.3bn hack of its platform by a group the FBI identified as being backed by North Korea .

The remaining 10% of tokens are less liquid, meaning they ⁠may take ​longer to buy, the company said in a post on X on Saturday. Co-CEO Richard Teng said separately that the company was “committed to covering the ⁠remaining 10%” and that “users will not bear the financial impact of this incident”.
How crypto hacking funds isolated North Korea’s nuclear programme
Binance suspended user withdrawals after the hack, but said on Sunday that some had resumed and would be rolled out in phases to ensure stability.
The announcement came as the FBI on Saturday confirmed earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack.

TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for The Interview, a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong-un.

“The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026,” the law enforcement agency said in a statement.
How big a deal is the $6.3bn Binance crypto heist, who did it, and are investments safe?

The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into Ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralised finance and instant swap services.
It said it was urging private sector entities “to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets”.

Teng said on Friday that the breach was a “complex attack” involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it ‌harder to trace and investigate.
Binance said it had set aside around $6.34bn of company funds to cover the losses.
“Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said.

The money spent re-buying tokens came from using part of its $1bn Secure Asset Fund for Users, a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches, as well as some ⁠of its Futures Insurance Fund, and the company’s own corporate treasury, it said ​on X.
The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.
Bitcoin plunged nearly 5% after the news of the hack, while Ethereum dropped nearly 6% and BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10%.

The sheer scale of the hack has put a spotlight on the capacity of North Korea – which faces extensive international sanctions over its nuclear and missile programmes – to find illicit means to capture revenue.
body_zh: 币安表示，FBI 称朝鲜是攻击幕后黑手，63 亿美元的黑客损失已被弥补 90% |币安
币安表示，FBI 称朝鲜是此次攻击的幕后黑手，63 亿美元黑客攻击造成的 90% 损失已得到赔偿
加密货币交易所表示，由于联邦调查局指责朝鲜国家支持的组织 TraderTraitor，提款将于周日开始恢复
加密货币交易所币安 (Binance) 表示，在 FBI 认定的一个受朝鲜支持的组织对其平台进行创纪录的 63 亿美元黑客攻击后，该交易所已替换了 90% 的被盗金额。
该公司周六在 X 上发布的一篇文章中表示，剩余 10% 的代币流动性较差，这意味着它们可能需要更长的时间才能购买。联席首席执行官邓强（Richard Teng）另外表示，该公司“致力于覆盖剩余的10%”，并且“用户不会承担此次事件的财务影响”。
加密黑客资金如何隔离朝鲜的核计划
黑客攻击后，币安暂停了用户提款，但周日表示，部分提款已经恢复，并将分阶段推出，以确保稳定性。
这一消息发布之际，美国联邦调查局 (FBI) 周六证实了私人调查员和分析师此前的怀疑，即一个名为 TraderTraitor 的朝鲜附属组织是此次黑客攻击的幕后黑手。
据信 TraderTraitor 是 Lazarus Group 的一部分，该集团在 2014 年因被指控入侵索尼影业以报复嘲笑朝鲜领导人金正恩的电影《采访》而声名狼藉。
“联邦调查局 (FBI) 发布的信息显示，朝鲜民主主义人民共和国（朝鲜）应对 2026 年 10 月 29 日左右从加密货币交易所币安盗窃超过 60 亿美元的虚拟资产负责，”该执法机构在一份声明中表示。
价值 63 亿美元的币安加密货币盗窃案到底有多大？是谁干的？投资安全吗？
联邦调查局补充说，它观察到“TraderTraitor 演员”将被盗资产转换为以太坊，并预计这些资产将通过使用去中心化金融和即时交换服务进行转换来进一步洗钱。
它表示，正在敦促私营部门实体“阻止与 TraderTraitor 行为者用来洗钱这些被盗资产的地址进行的交易或源自​​该地址的交易”。
滕周五表示，此次违规行为是一次“复杂的攻击”，涉及受感染的笔记本电脑和旨在删除其活动证据的恶意软件，从而使追踪和调查变得更加困难。
币安表示，已拨出约 63.4 亿美元的公司资金来弥补损失。
该公司表示：“我们的承诺保持不变：币安将全额承担本次事件中被盗资金的财务影响。”
该公司在 X 上表示，用于重新购买代币的资金来自使用其 10 亿美元的用户安全资产基金的一部分，这是该公司为在发生安全漏洞时保护客户而持有的比特币储备，以及部分期货保险基金和该公司自己的公司财务。
币安遭受攻击之际，许多观察家担心人工智能模型不断扩展的功能可能会损害密码学和 IT 安全协议。
黑客事件传出后，比特币暴跌近 5%，以太坊下跌近 6%，币安原生币安币 (BNB) 暴跌近 10%。
这次黑客攻击的规模之大让人们关注朝鲜寻找非法手段获取收入的能力——该国因其核计划和导弹计划而面临广泛的国际制裁。

title_en: How the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán
title_zh: 塞尔维亚总统武契奇的垮台如何反映了匈牙利奥尔班的垮台
summary: Defeat for Serbia's Aleksandar Vučiċ in last weekend's vote was a carbon copy of Viktor Orbán's fall in Hungary.
summary_zh: 塞尔维亚的亚历山大·武契奇(Aleksandar Vučiċ)在上周末的投票中落败，是维克多·欧尔班(Viktor Orbán)在匈牙利倒台的翻版。
body_en: When they met in northern Serbia last November, Serbian President Aleksandar Vučiċ and Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán could hardly have guessed they would both be out of power within a year.

Both were ousted by popular movements - Orbán fell first, in April, defeated by Péter Magyar's Tisza party. Then last Sunday a student movement less than two years old won Serbia's parliamentary elections by a landslide.

The Tisza party in Hungary and the Student List in Serbia look very different - Tisza is centred on the personality and energy of its leader, while the students in Serbia insist they have no leadership.

But the huge turnout - 79% in Hungary and 69% in Serbia, was driven by tech-savvy young people in both countries. They used AI tools to crunch numbers, identify threats to the vote, and mobilise tens of thousands of election monitors to prevent intimidation and electoral fraud by the governing parties.
Mobilisation of voters, and the role of election monitors, played a big role in the opposition victory in both countries.

Last weekend, the DE civic action group in Hungary sent 70 election monitors to Serbia, to work with students' movement representatives, visiting polling stations in the northern Serbian province of Vojvodina.
During the summer, even before the election was called, they held workshops to share their experience and methods from the Hungarian election with the Serbian students.

A key technique was to identify "infected" polling districts in advance - places where the surprisingly high number of votes for the governing party at previous elections suggested that voter intimidation or "chain voting" techniques were used.

"From around 16:00 on election day, we noticed groups of masked hooligans - Vučiċ supporters - gathering near voting stations," Péter Klemm, a student activist from Subotica, told the BBC. "So we sent mobile teams, and started filming everything."
Combined with the "stationary" monitors already in place, 20 to 30 volunteers at each threatened polling station acted as a strong deterrent, he believes, and prevented intimidation or fraud.

Orbán in Hungary, Vučiċ in Serbia, both looked invincible. Both were powerful leaders, in office for 16 and 14 years, who had taken over state institutions and established business empires overlapping the two countries.
Orban chose cheese, Vučiċ meat, when they sat down to a quick lunch of traditional burek pastries at a small, popular town centre bakery in Subotica almost a year ago.

They continued to a local winery, to talk about oil and other business deals - the planned Hungarian purchase of Serbia's Nis oil refinery. The two nationalist leaders found much in common, in business and politics, not least their friendship with Vladimir Putin in Russia and Chinese President Xi Jinping, and their strong support for Milorad Dodik, the separatist leader of the Bosnian Serbs.
A high-speed railway between Belgrade and Budapest is being built with Chinese finance and know-how.

The parallels between the fall from power of the two men are extraordinary. Aleksandar Vučiċ admitted defeat at exactly 21:30 on Sunday evening, just as Viktor Orbán did on 12 April. Few observers expected either leader to concede peacefully.

There has been speculation this week that Vučiċ spoke to Orbán twice on Sunday night to ask his advice - once before he conceded, and again at 23:15. And that Orbán convinced his Serbian ally not to use force.
Vučiċ denies that he spoke to Orbán before he made his announcement, but acknowledges the later conversation. Viktor Orbán, contacted by the BBC, declined to comment.

An hour before polls closed in Serbia, masked and hooded vigilantes took up position in central Belgrade. During voting, similar groups were photographed at many polling stations, and blocked by election monitors.

There is another strange numerical similarity. The Student List will have 140 seats in the 250-seat Serbian parliament, the same number Péter Magyar's Tisza party won in the 199-seat Hungarian parliament.
Magyar was the only European leader to ring the students directly to congratulate them that evening - and probably the only one who had their number.
body_zh: 去年11月，当塞尔维亚总统亚历山大·武契奇和匈牙利总理维克多·欧尔班在塞尔维亚北部会面时，他们几乎没有想到他们会在一年内双双下台。
两人都被民众运动赶下台——欧尔班首先于四月下台，被彼得·马扎尔领导的蒂萨党击败。然后上周日，一个成立不到两年的学生运动以压倒性优势赢得了塞尔维亚议会选举。
匈牙利的蒂萨党和塞尔维亚的学生名单看起来非常不同——蒂萨党以其领导人的个性和能量为中心，而塞尔维亚的学生则坚称他们没有领导权。
但匈牙利和塞尔维亚的投票率高达 79% 和 69%，这是由两国精通技术的年轻人推动的。他们使用人工智能工具来处理数据，识别投票威胁，并动员数以万计的选举监督员来防止执政党的恐吓和选举舞弊。
选民的动员和选举监督员的作用对两国反对派的胜利发挥了重要作用。
上周末，匈牙利DE公民行动组织向塞尔维亚派遣了70名选举监察员，与学生运动代表合作，视察了塞尔维亚北部伏伊伏丁那省的投票站。
夏天，甚至在选举之前，他们就举办了研讨会，与塞尔维亚学生分享匈牙利选举的经验和方法。
一项关键技术是提前识别“受感染”的投票区——在之前的选举中，执政党得票数惊人的高的地方表明选民使用了恐吓或“连锁投票”技术。
“从选举日 16:00 左右开始，我们注意到一群蒙面流氓 - Vučiċ 支持者 - 聚集在投票站附近，”来自苏博蒂察的学生活动人士彼得·克莱姆 (Péter Klemm) 告诉 BBC。 “所以我们派出了机动小组，开始拍摄一切。”
他认为，结合已经到位的“固定”监控器，每个受到威胁的投票站都有 20 至 30 名志愿者，起到了强大的威慑作用，并防止了恐吓或欺诈。
匈牙利的欧尔班、塞尔维亚的武契奇，看起来都是所向披靡。两人都是强大的领导人，分别在位16年和14年，接管了国家机构并建立了覆盖两国的商业帝国。
大约一年前，奥尔班在苏博蒂察市中心一家受欢迎的小型面包店坐下来享用传统的 burek 糕点时，选择了奶酪和 Vučiċ 肉。
他们继续前往当地一家酿酒厂，谈论石油和其他商业交易——匈牙利计划购买塞尔维亚的尼什炼油厂。这两位民族主义领导人在商业和政治方面有很多共同点，尤其是他们与俄罗斯弗拉基米尔·普京和中国国家主席习近平的友谊，以及对波斯尼亚塞族分离主义领导人米洛拉德·多迪克的大力支持。
贝尔格莱德和布达佩斯之间的高速铁路正在由中国的资金和技术建造。
两人的权力倒台之间有着非同寻常的相似之处。亚历山大·武契奇 (Aleksandar Vučiċ) 在周日晚上 21:30 整承认失败，正如维克多·欧尔班 (Viktor Orbán) 在 4 月 12 日所做的那样。很少有观察家预计两位领导人会和平让步。
本周有人猜测，武契奇在周日晚上两次与欧尔班通话征求他的建议——一次是在他认输之前，另一次是在 23:15。欧尔班说服他的塞尔维亚盟友不要使用武力。
武契奇否认他在宣布这一消息之前曾与欧尔班进行过交谈，但承认了后来的谈话。 BBC 联系了维克托·欧尔班 (Viktor Orbán)，但他拒绝置评。
塞尔维亚投票结束前一小时，戴着面具和头巾的治安维持者在贝尔格莱德市中心占据了位置。投票期间，类似的群体在许多投票站被拍到，并被选举监视器封锁。
还有另一个奇怪的数字相似性。学生名单将在塞尔维亚议会250个席位中占据140个席位，与彼得·马扎尔领导的蒂萨党在匈牙利议会199个席位中赢得的席位相同。
马扎尔是当晚唯一一位直接给学生打电话向他们表示祝贺的欧洲领导人，而且可能是唯一一位知道学生电话号码的领导人。

title_en: Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe
title_zh: 抗议活动在欧洲蔓延，数千人在巴黎示威
summary: More than 320,000 people demonstrated across France against the rising cost of living and poor public services, with clashes between some protesters and police.
summary_zh: 法国各地超过32万人举行示威活动，抗议生活成本上涨和公共服务不佳，一些抗议者之间发生冲突
body_en: Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe - BBC News
Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe
Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe Close
Hundreds of thousands of protesters demonstrated across France as the country prepares for a general strike in the coming days.
In Paris, police fired tear gas and clashed with protesters in a third weekend of nationwide demonstrations against the rising cost of living and poor public services.
More than 320,000 people took to the streets around the country and at least 290 protesters were arrested, according to France's interior ministry. Police say about 70,000 demonstrated in Paris.
The authorities prepared extensively to avoid a repeat of the violence, rioting and looting that happened two weeks ago.
Protests also took place in Albania, Germany and Italy as youth take to the streets across Europe, the BBC's correspondent James Waterhouse reports.

title_en: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
title_zh: 加密货币公司 Binance 承担 63 亿美元黑客攻击后 90% 的损失
summary: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) says North Korea was responsible for the hack.
summary_zh: 美国联邦调查局 (FBI) 表示，朝鲜应对此次黑客攻击负责。
body_en: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has covered 90% of the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) assets stolen in a hack on Thursday.
The remaining 10% may take longer to source in the required amounts, the company added.
Binance has consistently pledged to cover 100% of the losses from what is suspected to be crypto's biggest hack on record and said it has set aside more than $6.34bn in company funds to do so.
"Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users," the company said in a statement on Saturday.
In an update on Sunday, Binance said withdrawals had been restored on several of its networks, after they were suspended following the hack.
It previously said withdrawals would be resumed in phases.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said on Saturday that North Korea was responsible for the attack.

The FBI said it had observed hackers converting stolen assets into a type of cryptocurrency called Ethereum and that it is expected that the assets will then be converted again using decentralised finance and instant swap services.

Two analytics firms previously told the BBC they had robust intelligence pointing to North Korean state-backed hacking unit the Lazarus Group, also known as TraderTraitor - which was specifically named by the FBI - as the likely culprits.
Binance said it had replenished the stolen assets using various funds and its own corporate treasury.
All holdings of the cryptocurrencies bitcoin, Ethereum and Tether are covered, along with seven other widely-traded crypto assets, the company said.
From Bitcoin to Binance: Crypto terms and what they mean
The hack is believed to be the largest in history, eclipsing the record of a $1.5bn heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025 - for which the FBI also said North Korea was responsible.
North Korea has always denied involvement in these attacks.

Binance's initial investigation suggested an engineer's laptop was compromised, which allowed access to unauthorised withdrawals, but a later update said they had uncovered "additional points of breach".

Richard Teng, Binance's co-chief executive officer, said the hack was carried out by more than one person, and the hackers used sophisticated methods to hide their tracks, such as a "self-destruct mechanism".
On Friday, the company said it had frozen around $3bn of stolen assets after working with law enforcement, intelligence firms and partners.

The investigation is ongoing, it added. The US Secret Service said on Friday it is "working around the clock" with private sector partners "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover funds" stolen from Binance.
Binance, founded in China in 2017, lets users buy, sell and trade digital assets - it is estimated to have hundreds of millions of users worldwide.
Crypto is a digital asset, which doesn't exist physically and is instead accessed via digital wallets or computers.
body_zh: 全球最大的加密货币交易所币安表示，周四在一次黑客攻击中被盗的 63 亿美元（47 亿英镑）资产中的 90% 已得到赔偿。
该公司补充说，剩下的 10% 可能需要更长时间才能获得所需数量。
币安一直承诺将承担 100% 的损失，该损失被怀疑是有史以来最大的加密货币黑客攻击，并表示已拨出超过 63.4 亿美元的公司资金来做到这一点。
该公司在周六的一份声明中表示：“币安将承担这些被盗资金的财务影响，而不是我们的用户。”
币安在周日的更新中表示，其多个网络在遭受黑客攻击后被暂停，提款现已恢复。
该公司此前曾表示，提款将分阶段恢复。
美国联邦调查局 (FBI) 周六表示，朝鲜应对此次黑客攻击负责。
美国联邦调查局表示，它观察到黑客将被盗资产转换为一种名为以太坊的加密货币，预计这些资产随后将使用去中心化金融和即时交换服务再次转换。
两家分析公司此前告诉 BBC，他们掌握的可靠情报表明，朝鲜国家支持的黑客组织 Lazarus Group（也称为 TraderTraitor）可能是罪魁祸首。
币安表示，它已使用各种资金和自己的公司财务补充了被盗的资产。
该公司表示，所有持有的加密货币比特币、以太坊和 Tether 以及其他七种广泛交易的加密资产都包含在内。
从比特币到币安：加密术语及其含义
此次黑客攻击被认为是历史上规模最大的一次，打破了 2025 年 Bybit 交易所被盗 15 亿美元的记录，而联邦调查局 (FBI) 也表示朝鲜对此负有责任。
朝鲜一直否认参与了这些袭击。
币安的初步调查显示，一名工程师的笔记本电脑遭到入侵，导致未经授权的提款行为，但后来的更新称，他们发现了“其他漏洞”。
币安联席首席执行官理查德·滕（Richard Teng）表示，这次黑客攻击是由不止一个人实施的，黑客使用了复杂的方法来隐藏自己的踪迹，例如“自毁机制”。
周五，该公司表示，在与执法部门、情报公司和合作伙伴合作后，已冻结了约 30 亿美元的被盗资产。
它补充说，调查正在进行中。美国特勤局周五表示，它正在与私营部门合作伙伴“昼夜不停地工作”，以“识别、冻结、追踪和追回”从币安被盗的资金。
币安于 2017 年在中国成立，允许用户购买、出售和交易数字资产 - 据估计在全球拥有数亿用户。
加密货币是一种数字资产，它并不实际存在，而是通过数字钱包或计算机访问。

title_en: Where are the most expensive midterm races and who is funding them?
title_zh: 最昂贵的中期选举在哪里？谁资助它们？
summary: Senate races in Texas, Michigan and Ohio rank among the most expensive in this year's midterm cycle.
summary_zh: 德克萨斯州、密歇根州和俄亥俄州的参议员竞选是今年中期选举中成本最高的。
body_en: Share Where are the most expensive midterm races and who is funding them? on social media
On Tuesday, voters across the United States will head to the polls to cast a ballot in the 2026 midterm elections.
The race is expected to serve as a referendum on Republican President Donald Trump’s job performance so far, at the halfway mark of his second term.

list 2 of 4 Trump’s beef tariff pause sparks anger among US ranchers
list 3 of 4 Hackers target US campaign finance system days before midterm elections
list 4 of 4 Tracking the money: The biggest donors in the 2026 US midterm elections
Maintaining the Republican majority in both chambers of Congress will be key for the success of Trump’s legislative agenda in his final two years.
But control of the US Congress could hinge on a handful of closely contested Senate and House of Representatives races nationwide.

Candidates, political parties and outside groups are pouring hundreds of millions of dollars into the contests, with major political action committees (PACs), including those associated with billionaire tech CEO Elon Musk, fuelling the spending battle.
Which races are costing the most, and who is bankrolling the fight for control of Congress?
This year’s midterms are projected to break records for the total amount of spending in a political election cycle.
Among the most expensive individual races are those for toss-up Senate seats. Battles in Texas, Ohio and Michigan rank as the costliest.

The race in Texas, for instance, is projected to shatter spending records for a US Senate race. A Democrat has not won statewide office in Texas since 1994, but Senate hopeful James Talarico aims to break the left-wing party’s losing streak.

Nearly every major poll suggests Talarico has a slim lead over his Republican rival, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton. CNN, for instance, projected in late October that Talarico had 49 percent support, compared with Paxton’s 43 percent.
Interest in the race is high. The Texas secretary of state’s office released data indicating that nearly 4.5 million Texans cast their ballots in the first week of early voting alone.
This election cycle, candidate campaigns and outside groups have spent more than $534m on the Texas race.

Talarico has outpaced his opponent in fundraising. The Democrat has raised $146m, compared with Paxton’s roughly $22m. However, Paxton has benefitted from significantly more outside spending, with nearly $300m spent on his behalf, compared with about $80m for Talarico.
Some $37m for Paxton has come from MAGA Inc, a super PAC aligned with President Donald Trump.
Ohio is considered the second-most expensive Senate race this cycle. More than $435m has been spent so far on the contest between Democrat Sherrod Brown and Republican Jon Husted.

哪些竞选成本最高？谁为国会控制权之争提供资金？
今年的中期选举预计将打破政治选举周期的支出总额记录。
最昂贵的个人竞选是参议员席位的竞选。德克萨斯州、俄亥俄州和密歇根州的战斗成本最高。
例如，德克萨斯州的竞选预计将打破美国参议院竞选的支出记录。自 1994 年以来，民主党还没有在德克萨斯州赢得过全州的职位，但参议院候选人詹姆斯·塔拉里科 (James Talarico) 的目标是打破左翼政党的连败纪录。
几乎所有主要民意调查都显示，塔拉里科以微弱优势领先于他的共和党对手、得克萨斯州总检察长肯·帕克斯顿。例如，CNN 在 10 月底预测塔拉里科的支持率为 49%，而帕克斯顿的支持率为 43%。
人们对比赛的兴趣很高。德克萨斯州国务卿办公室公布的数据显示，仅提前投票第一周就有近450万德克萨斯人投票。
本次选举周期，候选人竞选活动和外部团体在德克萨斯州竞选上花费了超过 5.34 亿美元。
塔拉里科在筹款方面超过了对手。民主党筹集了 1.46 亿美元，而帕克斯顿筹集了大约 2200 万美元。然而，Paxton 受益于更多的外部支出，为他花费了近 3 亿美元，而 Talarico 的花费约为 8000 万美元。
Paxton 的约 3700 万美元来自 MAGA Inc，这是一家与唐纳德·特朗普总统结盟的超级政治行动委员会。
俄亥俄州被认为是本周期第二昂贵的参议院竞选。迄今为止，民主党人谢罗德·布朗和共和党人乔恩·赫斯特德之间的竞争已花费超过 4.35 亿美元。

title_en: 'We came back from hell', say Ukrainians after years in Russia-occupied front-line city
title_zh: 在俄罗斯占领的前线城市生活多年后，乌克兰人说：“我们从地狱回来了”
summary: One evacuated couple says they crossed minefields in Oleshky in search of food.
summary_zh: 一对被疏散的夫妇说，他们穿过奥列什基的雷区寻找食物。
body_en: By Dan Johnson , Ukraine correspondent , Reporting from Chernihiv , Mariana Matveichuk , Reporting from Chernihiv and Amy Walker
Warning: This story contains graphic content.
Olha has one word to describe what life has been like in the front-line city of Oleshky over the past few years: "Horror".
Disembarking alongside her from a coach in the Ukrainian region of Chernihiv with their immediate family and dog, her husband Viacheslav put it this way: "We came back from hell."

The couple were among hundreds of residents evacuated from the Russian-occupied city who crossed into northern Ukraine via Belarus on Saturday, many reuniting with loved ones they had not seen for years.
Oleshky, seized by Russia during the first few days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022, is trapped on one side by the Dnipro River and on the other side by Russian forces.

Olha and Viacheslav had lived there with their son and daughter, both in their 30s. Even as the shelling around them intensified, they feared that trying to escape could be even more dangerous, with routes mined and subject to drone attack.

As supplies dwindled, the couple said they made an attempt to find food by crossing through minefields earlier this month. "People were stepping on mines, dying and being maimed, all just to survive," Olha told the BBC.
Those who were too afraid to go out in the city had resorted to cooking garden weeds to survive.
"We saw that the situation wasn't getting any better, so we realised we had to get out," Olha said.

That opportunity came earlier this week when a humanitarian ceasefire, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, took effect in the Kherson region, providing the first few days of peace in the area for four years and allowing Oleshky residents to evacuate.
Up to 6,000 people, including 200 children, were believed to still be living in Oleshky and its surrounding areas, with 1,700 in the city itself.
Residents had a four-hour window on Friday to leave, with a convoy of 25 buses brought in for up to 750 evacuees, along with ambulances for people with limited mobility.
After travelling through Russian-occupied territory to southern Russia, then flying to Belarus, evacuees arrived on buses to a military facility in Chernihiv on Saturday.
On the tarmac, where evacuees were processed before travelling onwards, some elderly residents were so weak they had to be carried on stretchers.
As Mykhailo Palii arrived, his daughters Dasha and Anya, who thought they might never see him again, sprinted across the tarmac screaming and crying.
After an emotional embrace, Palii described a glimpse of life in Oleshky, although he said he had, until then, kept many of the details from his family.
"A hole was blown into the bathroom," he said. "There were drone attacks and missile strikes. It happened, but I didn't tell them about it because I knew they would worry."

Tetiana and Volodymyr, a couple carrying a cat when they arrived in Chernihiv, said their entire home was burned down three years ago, and they had been living in the abandoned house of a neighbour since.

For them, leaving as soon as it was safe to do so was an easy decision. "There's nothing for us to regret leaving. We don't have relatives there. Our children are married and don't live with us in the city," said Tetiana.
body_zh: 作者：丹·约翰逊，乌克兰记者，切尔尼戈夫报道，玛丽安娜·马特维丘克，切尔尼戈夫报道和艾米·沃克
警告：这个故事包含图形内容。
奥尔哈用一个词来形容过去几年奥列什基一线城市的生活：“恐怖”。
与她一起从乌克兰切尔尼戈夫地区的一辆长途汽车上下来的时候，她的丈夫维亚切斯拉夫带着直系亲属和狗，这样说道：“我们从地狱回来了。”
这对夫妇是周六从俄罗斯占领的城市撤离的数百名居民之一，他们于周六经白俄罗斯进入乌克兰北部，其中许多人与多年未见的亲人团聚。
奥列什基在 2022 年 2 月全面入侵的头几天被俄罗斯占领，一侧被第聂伯河围困，另一侧被俄罗斯军队围困。
奥尔哈 (Olha) 和维亚切斯拉夫 (Viacheslav) 带着他们的儿子和女儿住在那里，他们都是 30 多岁。尽管周围的炮击愈演愈烈，他们还是担心试图逃跑可能会更加危险，因为路线上布满了地雷，而且容易受到无人机袭击。
随着供应减少，这对夫妇表示，他们本月早些时候试图穿过雷区寻找食物。奥尔哈告诉英国广播公司：“人们踩到地雷，要么死亡，要么受伤，这一切只是为了生存。”
那些不敢进城的人只能靠煮菜园里的杂草来维持生计。
“我们看到情况没有任何好转，所以我们意识到我们必须离开，”奥尔哈说。
本周早些时候，这个机会来了，在美国第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普的斡旋下，人道主义停火在赫尔松地区生效，为该地区带来了四年来最初几天的和平，并允许奥列什基居民撤离。
据信仍有多达 6,000 人（其中包括 200 名儿童）居住在奥列什基及其周边地区，其中 1,700 人居住在该市。
周五，居民有四个小时的时间离开，一支由 25 辆巴士组成的车队运载了多达 750 名疏散人员，并为行动不便的人提供了救护车。
经过俄罗斯占领的领土前往俄罗斯南部，然后飞往白俄罗斯后，撤离人员于周六乘坐巴士抵达切尔尼戈夫的一处军事设施。
在停机坪上，疏散人员在继续前行之前接受了处理，一些老年居民非常虚弱，不得不用担架抬着。
当米凯洛·帕利到达时，他的女儿达莎和安雅以为自己可能再也见不到他了，尖叫着哭着冲过停机坪。
在一次激动人心的拥抱之后，帕利描述了奥列什基生活的一瞥，尽管他说在那之前他一直向家人隐瞒了许多细节。
“浴室被炸了一个洞，”他说。 “发生了无人机袭击和导弹袭击。这种事确实发生了，但我没有告诉他们，因为我知道他们会担心。”
Tetiana 和 Volodymyr 是一对夫妇，他们抵达切尔尼戈夫时带着一只猫。他们说，三年前他们的整个房子都被烧毁了，从那以后他们就一直住在邻居的废弃房子里。
对他们来说，在安全的情况下尽快离开是一个简单的决定。 “离开没有什么让我们后悔的。我们在那里没有亲戚。我们的孩子已经结婚了，不和我们一起住在城里，”特蒂亚娜说。

title_en: Bangladesh forms wage board as garment workers protest
title_zh: 服装工人抗议孟加拉国成立工资委员会
summary: Demonstrations held in industrial cities as workers demand wage increase as cost of living rises.
summary_zh: 由于生活成本上升，工人们要求增加工资，工业城市举行示威活动。
body_en: Bangladesh forms wage board as garment workers protest | Labour Rights News | Al Jazeera
Share Bangladesh forms wage board as garment workers protest on social media
Bangladesh has formed a new wage board to review the minimum wage for garment workers as it tries to quell a protest movement that has disrupted key industrial hubs.

Despite the announcement on Sunday, thousands of workers demanding higher wages continued protesting around the capital, Dhaka. Clashes were reported with police, who fired tear gas and sound grenades.

The garment sector is the backbone of Bangladesh’s export-driven economy , employing millions of workers and generating the bulk of the country’s foreign earnings.

Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($242), more than double the current wage of 12,500 taka ($101). They said the rising costs of food, housing, transport and healthcare have sharply eroded their purchasing power.
The six-member board is to include representatives of the government, workers and factory owners and is tasked with determining a new minimum wage.
“The issue of forming the wage board has been resolved. There will be no more problems now,” Ministry of Labour and Employment adviser M Sakhawat Hossain Chowdhury told reporters.
“The workers should return to work and work smoothly,” he added.

Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury warned that prolonged factory closures and production disruptions could delay export shipments and payments from international buyers, creating further difficulties for manufacturers and workers alike.

The protests began on Saturday and prompted about 30 garment factories on the outskirts of Dhaka to declare holidays, according to Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of the Ashulia Industrial Police.
Clashes between workers and police in Ashulia injured several people, including police officers, police said.
Bangladesh’s garment industry is the world’s largest after China’s, contributing about 10 percent of gross domestic product.

Manufacturers, however, said the sector is facing mounting challenges, including rising production costs, periodic gas and electricity shortages, and uncertainty in energy markets linked to tensions in the Middle East during the United States-Israel war on Iran.
body_zh: 服装工人抗议，孟加拉国成立工资委员会劳工权利新闻 |半岛电视台
服装工人在社交媒体上抗议，孟加拉国成立工资委员会
孟加拉国成立了一个新的工资委员会，以审查服装工人的最低工资，试图平息扰乱主要工业中心的抗议运动。
尽管周日宣布了这一消息，但数千名要求提高工资的工人仍在首都达卡周围举行抗议活动。据报道，与警察发生了冲突，警察发射了催泪瓦斯和声波手榴弹。

服装行业是孟加拉国出口驱动型经济的支柱，雇用了数百万工人并创造了该国大部分外汇收入。
工人们要求最低月工资为 30,000 塔卡（242 美元），是当前工资 12,500 塔卡（101 美元）的两倍多。他们表示，食品、住房、交通和医疗保健成本的上涨严重削弱了他们的购买力。
这个由六名成员组成的委员会将包括政府、工人和工厂主的代表，其任务是确定新的最低工资。
劳工和就业部顾问萨哈瓦特·侯赛因·乔杜里 (M Sakhawat Hossain Chowdhury) 告诉记者：“组建工资委员会的问题已经解决。现在不会再有问题了。”
他补充说：“工人们应该重返工作岗位并顺利工作。”
劳工和就业部长阿里弗尔·哈克·乔杜里警告说，工厂长期关闭和生产中断可能会延迟出口发货和国际买家的付款，给制造商和工人带来进一步的困难。
阿苏利亚工业警察局长穆罕默德·莫米努尔·伊斯兰·布伊扬 (Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan) 表示，抗议活动于周六开始，导致达卡郊区约 30 家服装厂宣布放假。
警方称，阿苏利亚工人与警察之间的冲突造成多人受伤，其中包括警察。
孟加拉国的服装业是仅次于中国的全球最大服装业，约占国内生产总值的10%。
然而，制造商表示，该行业正面临着越来越大的挑战，包括生产成本上升、天然气和电力周期性短缺，以及美以对伊朗战争期间中东紧张局势导致的能源市场不确定性。

title_en: Donald Trump loses allies after elections in Serbia and Brazil
title_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普在塞尔维亚和巴西大选后失去盟友
summary: Flavio Bolsonaro failed to gain power, Aleksandar Vucic was voted out of office, and even Benjamin Netanyahu's position has weakened. An unhappy US President Trump is crying electoral fraud.
summary_zh: 弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗未能掌权，亚历山大·武契奇被投票下台，甚至本杰明·内塔尼亚胡的地位也被削弱。不开心的美国公关
body_en: The midterm elections in the United States are just around the corner: On Tuesday, November 3, American voters will choose their representatives to the US Congress. The right-wing-conservative Republican party of President Donald Trump currently has a majority in both chambers.

But in other parts of the world election results are already in. The majority of voters in both Serbia and Brazil cast their ballots for left-wing parties. Those results will not influence the midterms in the US, but the victories of the Student List in Serbia and the incumbent president, Luiz Inacio "Lula" da Silva , in Brazil are bad news for Trump all the same.
In Serbia, he has lost an important European ally in outgoing president Aleksandar Vucic . And in Brazil, the Trump camp had been hoping Flavio Bolsonaro would triumph.

"Trump was a strong supporter of both Jair Bolsonaro , the Trump-like figure who served as president before Lula defeated him in 2022, and of his son Flavio," says Lawrence J. Haas, a senior fellow for US foreign policy at the American Foreign Policy Council, who was communications director for Al Gore, Bill Clinton's vice president, in the 1990s. "Trump wasn't happy about the defeat of either Bolsonaro," he continues, "and he doesn't feel warmly toward Lula. So relations will remain cool at best."
Trump declared Brazilian election looked "rigged"

Flavio Bolsonaro is under investigation in Brazil for alleged corruption and money laundering. After losing the election, he fled the country for Florida . The US State Department granted him and his family entry visas in spite of the pending legal action.

Bolsonaro has refused to concede defeat. Instead, he claims there were irregularities in the vote. This is very reminiscent of Trump, who continues to claim – falsely – that Joe Biden and the Democratic Party "stole" the US election in 2020. Trump's comments on Bolsonaro's defeat sounded very familiar. "It looked like another rigged election, frankly," the US president said on Monday. "Elections have to be indisputable – and it looked very bad to me."

Aleksandar Vucic had ruled Serbia as president with an iron fist since 2017. He resigned just before these elections in order to stand as prime minister, a role he previously held from 2014 to 2017. Vucic has commented in the past that he and President Trump are like-minded people. Trump's eldest son, Donald Jr., visited Vucic in Belgrade shortly before the US presidential elections in November 2024, and again a few months later.

The US Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC), which is closely connected with Trump's MAGA ("Make America Great Again") movement, recently announced that it was organizing a meeting in Belgrade in November, at which Vucic was to be a keynote speaker. It is unclear whether this is still the case.

Another thing Vucic and Trump have in common is that the soon-to-be-ex-president of Serbia has a much more positive attitude toward Russian president Vladimir Putin than do most other European heads of state. Vucic did not join EU countries in imposing sanctions on Russia after it launched its war of aggression against Ukraine . Belgrade still buys Russian raw materials, and Serbian state media under Vucic presented a more positive image of Russia than of the EU.

Trump also seems increasingly inclined toward Moscow. His special envoy Steve Witkoff recently described Putin as a " humanitarian ," while, in an interview, Trump himself openly admitted that he got on better with Putin than with the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy . The end of the Vucic government now means that Trump has lost one of his few allies in Europe who takes a similar view.
Is Trump trying to end the war in Ukraine, or helping Putin win it?

There's still a chance of an outcome in the Israeli elections that might be to Trump's liking. With more than 96% of votes counted, the right-wing bloc led by prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu is in the lead. However, Trump ally Netanyahu has lost his majority, and the coalition negotiations will be very difficult.

Trump and Netanyahu have been close allies since well before February this year, when they joined forces to launch a war against Iran. In 2018, during his first term in office, Trump moved the US embassy in Israel from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem. This was controversial, because both Israel and Palestinians claim Jerusalem as their capital. Netanyahu's camp welcomed the decision.

Today, the United States is still by far Israel's most important partner, while Israel is an important regional ally for the US. It is not clear what their relationship would be like with a different Israeli government. If Netanyahu remains in power , little, if anything, will change.

With Vucic's defeat, Trump has lost a loyal ally. And Lula's victory means, for him, that a disagreeable president remains in power. None of this is good for Trump, but foreign policy analyst Haas said it won't influence the important midterm elections in his country. "Americans will be voting [...] on the basis of issues that affect them, and how they feel about the party in power."

But this doesn't bode well for Trump, either. "Trump has the lowest approval rating of any president on the eve of a mid-term election since Harry Truman in 1946," Haas explained. "Americans are very concerned about issues of affordability, [and] they strongly oppose the US-Iran war."
Benjamin Alvarez Gruber in Miami contributed to this report, which was originally written in German.
body_zh: 美国中期选举在即：11月3日星期二，美国选民将选出美国国会代表。唐纳德·特朗普总统领导的右翼保守共和党目前在参众两院均占多数。
但在世界其他地区，选举结果已经出来。塞尔维亚和巴西的大多数选民都把票投给了左翼政党。这些结果不会影响美国的中期选举，但塞尔维亚学生名单和巴西现任总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·“卢拉”·达席尔瓦的胜利对特朗普来说仍然是坏消息。
在塞尔维亚，他失去了即将卸任的总统亚历山大·武契奇（Aleksandar Vucic）这一重要的欧洲盟友。在巴西，特朗普阵营一直希望弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗能够获胜。

美国外交政策委员会美国外交政策高级研究员劳伦斯·哈斯 (Lawrence J. Haas) 表示，“特朗普是贾尔·博尔索纳罗 (Jair Bolsonaro) 和他儿子弗拉维奥 (Flavio) 的坚定支持者。贾尔·博尔索纳罗是与特朗普类似的人物，在 2022 年卢拉击败特朗普之前曾担任总统。 “特朗普对博尔索纳罗的失败并不满意，”他继续说道，“他对卢拉也没有热情。因此，两国关系最多只能保持冷淡。”
特朗普宣称巴西选举看起来“被操纵”
弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗因涉嫌腐败和洗钱而在巴西接受调查。选举失败后，他逃离该国前往佛罗里达州。尽管法律诉讼尚未结束，美国国务院仍向他和他的家人发放了入境签证。
博尔索纳罗拒绝承认失败。相反，他声称投票存在违规行为。这很容易让人想起特朗普，他继续错误地声称乔·拜登和民主党“偷走了”2020年美国大选。特朗普对博尔索纳罗落败的评论听起来非常熟悉。 “坦率地说，这看起来像是另一场被操纵的选举，”美国总统周一表示。 “选举必须是无可争议的——但对我来说，这看起来非常糟糕。”

亚历山大·武契奇自 2017 年以来一直以总统身份铁腕统治塞尔维亚。他在选举前夕辞职，以担任总理，此前他曾在 2014 年至 2017 年担任总理。武契奇过去曾表示，他和特朗普总统是志同道合的人。特朗普的长子小唐纳德在 2024 年 11 月美国总统大选前夕访问了贝尔格莱德的武契奇，几个月后又再次访问。
与特朗普的MAGA（“让美国再次伟大”）运动密切相关的美国保守党政治行动会议（CPAC）最近宣布将于11月在贝尔格莱德组织一次会议，武契奇将在会上发表主旨演讲。目前尚不清楚情况是否仍然如此。
武契奇和特朗普的另一个共同点是，这位即将成为塞尔维亚前总统的人对俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京的态度比大多数其他欧洲国家元首要积极得多。在俄罗斯发动侵略乌克兰战争后，武契奇没有与欧盟国家一起对俄罗斯实施制裁。贝尔格莱德仍然购买俄罗斯原材料，武契奇领导下的塞尔维亚官方媒体对俄罗斯的形象比对欧盟的形象更为积极。
特朗普似乎也越来越倾向于莫斯科。他的特使史蒂夫·威特科夫最近将普京描述为“人道主义者”，而特朗普本人在接受采访时公开承认，他与普京的关系比与乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基的关系更好。武契奇政府的终结现在意味着特朗普失去了他在欧洲为数不多的持类似观点的盟友之一。
特朗普是想结束乌克兰战争，还是帮助普京赢得战争？
以色列选举仍有可能出现特朗普喜欢的结果。目前计票已超过 96%，总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡领导的右翼集团处于领先地位。然而，特朗普的盟友内塔尼亚胡已经失去了多数席位，联合政府谈判将会非常困难。
特朗普和内塔尼亚胡早在今年二月联手对伊朗发动战争之前就一直是亲密盟友。 2018年，特朗普在第一任期内将美国驻以色列大使馆从特拉维夫迁至耶路撒冷。这是有争议的，因为以色列和巴勒斯坦都声称耶路撒冷是他们的首都。内塔尼亚胡阵营对这一决定表示欢迎。
如今，美国仍然是以色列最重要的伙伴，而以色列则是美国重要的地区盟友。目前尚不清楚他们与不同的以色列政府的关系会是什么样。如果内塔尼亚胡继续掌权，即使有什么变化，也不会发生什么变化。
随着武契奇的落选，特朗普失去了一个忠实的盟友。对卢拉来说，他的胜利意味着一位令人讨厌的总统继续掌权。这一切对特朗普都没有好处，但外交政策分析师哈斯表示，这不会影响他的国家重要的中期选举。 “美国人将根据影响他们的问题以及他们对执政党的看法进行投票。”
但这对特朗普来说也不是好兆头。哈斯解释说：“自 1946 年哈里·杜鲁门以来，特朗普在中期选举前夕的支持率是所有总统中最低的。” “美国人非常关心负担能力问题，[并且]他们强烈反对美伊战争。”

body_en: Turkey has been hit by powerful thunderstorms and a fatal tornado this week with more heavy rain expected

Heavy rain and strong winds will continue to affect parts of south-eastern Europe and Turkey over the next few days, as an area of low pressure in the region has allowed for the formation of powerful thunderstorms. During a particularly intense thunderstorm in Antalya, a coastal city in the south-west of Turkey, the formation of a tornado resulted in the deaths of four construction workers on Tuesday. Authorities in Greece and Turkey have released severe rainfall and flooding warnings, as a further 100-150mm (nearly 4-6in) of rain is expected this week in central Greece and western parts of Turkey, with locally higher totals possible.

Travelling eastwards towards south Asia, strong winds and heavy rainfall have swept across the Indian regions of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh as Cyclone Arnab made landfall. With wind gusts in excess of 85mph (140km/h) and rainfall totals in some regions exceeding 200mm, the severe storm has prompted mass evacuations of more than 180,000 people, as well as widespread disruption to energy and transport infrastructure. The cyclone will weaken as it continues to traverse northwards over the coming days, though will continue to deliver heavy rain to parts of northern and central India as it does so.
body_zh: 土耳其本周遭遇强烈雷暴和致命龙卷风袭击，预计还会有更多大雨
未来几天，大雨和强风将继续影响东南欧和土耳其的部分地区，因为该地区的低压区域导致了强大的雷暴的形成。周二，土耳其西南部沿海城市安塔利亚遭遇特别强烈的雷暴，龙卷风的形成导致四名建筑工人死亡。希腊和土耳其当局已发布严重降雨和洪水警告，预计希腊中部和土耳其西部地区本周将进一步降雨 100-150 毫米（近 4-6 英寸），局部地区降雨总量可能更高。
随着气旋“阿纳布”登陆，向东向南亚移动，强风和强降雨席卷了印度奥里萨邦和安得拉邦地区。阵风超过 85 英里/小时（140 公里/小时），部分地区降雨量超过 200 毫米，这场严重风暴已导致超过 18 万人大规模疏散，能源和交通基础设施也受到广泛破坏。未来几天，气旋将继续向北移动，强度将减弱，但仍将给印度北部和中部部分地区带来大雨。

title_en: Spain train disaster clouds Sánchez chances of re-election
title_zh: 西班牙火车灾难给桑切斯连任的机会蒙上阴影
summary: The Spanish PM is hit by a succession of crises just weeks before a snap general election.
summary_zh: 距离提前大选仅几周，西班牙首相遭遇一系列危机。
body_en: Southern and Eastern Europe correspondent , Reporting from Toledo
The breaking news from Spain this week was shocking but also shockingly familiar: another collision on the high-speed rail line south from Madrid, with reports of dozens killed.
It is just nine months since two trains crashed near Cordoba, killing 46 people. Now 69 bodies have been recovered here in central Spain, from wreckage strewn over the tracks and down an embankment.
For the victims' families it is devastating; a personal tragedy.

But it is also a national disaster that has shattered confidence in the country's rail network and the Socialist-led government of Pedro Sánchez. It is playing out just weeks before the snap general election he called.
The formal investigation into the Toledo train disaster has only just been launched but the government has been quick to take control of the narrative.
From the first hours after the collision, Transport Minister Oscar Puente began suggesting "human error" was to blame, batting responsibility as far as possible from the cabinet.
On Friday, he appeared before the press for a second time to set out what he called the "objective facts" of the crash and counter a surge of criticism against the government.
The opposition People's Party (PP) is among those calling for his resignation as a "moral" and "ethical" move.
Instead after expressing "huge pain and sadness" for the victims, Puente went on the offensive.
He rejected talk of chronic underinvestment in infrastructure and insisted that Spain's high-speed signalling safety system, the LZB, was neither old nor inadequate: Germany and Austria use the same.
In Spain, it has already failed 170 times so far this year, he revealed, but called that "normal" and around the EU average.
The problem surrounds what happens next - when the system fails and control of the line shifts to manual.
In this case, the minister highlighted a series of human errors that proved catastrophic.
Crucially, at one point a controller instructed a stalled train to restart, clearing it to advance at up to 160km/h (100 mph) even though a second train was stuck on the line up ahead.
The impending collision was clear from audio calls and on big screens in the control centre in Madrid.
"They worked. We checked. They could see what was happening," Puente confirmed. But the advancing train was never ordered to stop.
So would he take personal and political responsibility anyway, and resign? Puente called it his "duty", rather, to remain as minister.
"I'll face up to things, explain, elucidate," he countered. "I'll think how to improve the system, and give confidence to those who want to travel by train and feel calm and safe."
"This is not only a very serious accident, but the second in a very short time," Paco Camas of the pollster Ipsos points out.
body_zh: 南欧和东欧记者，托莱多报道
本周来自西班牙的突发新闻令人震惊，但也令人震惊地熟悉：马德里以南的高铁线上再次发生碰撞，据报道有数十人死亡。
距离科尔多瓦附近两列火车相撞、造成 46 人死亡仅九个月。目前，西班牙中部已从散布在铁轨和路堤上的残骸中找到了 69 具尸体。
对于受害者家属来说，这是毁灭性的；个人悲剧。
但这也是一场全国性灾难，粉碎了人们对该国铁路网络和佩德罗·桑切斯领导的社会党政府的信心。就在他呼吁提前大选的几周前，这场比赛即将上演。
对托莱多火车灾难的正式调查才刚刚启动，但政府很快就控制了局势。
从碰撞发生后的最初几个小时起，交通部长奥斯卡·普恩特就开始暗示“人为失误”是事故的罪魁祸首，并尽可能地推卸内阁的责任。
周五，他第二次出现在媒体面前，阐述了他所谓的坠机事件的“客观事实”，并反驳了针对政府的批评浪潮。
反对党人民党是呼吁他辞职的人士之一，认为这是“道德”和“道德”的举动。
在向受害者表达“巨大的痛苦和悲伤”后，普恩特转而采取攻势。
他否认了基础设施投资长期不足的说法，并坚称西班牙的高速信号安全系统 LZB 既不陈旧也不不足：德国和奥地利也使用同样的系统。
他透露，今年迄今为止，西班牙已经失败了 170 次，但他称这“正常”，接近欧盟平均水平。
问题围绕着接下来会发生什么——当系统发生故障并且生产线的控制转为手动时。
在这种情况下，部长强调了一系列被证明是灾难性的人为错误。
至关重要的是，在某一时刻，管制员指示一列停滞的列车重新启动，使其以 160 公里/小时（100 英里/小时）的速度前进，尽管前面有第二列列车被困在线路上。
从音频通话和马德里控制中心的大屏幕上可以清楚地看到即将发生的碰撞。
“他们工作了。我们检查了。他们可以看到发生了什么，”普恩特证实。但行进中的火车从未被命令停止。
那么他无论如何都会承担个人和政治责任并辞职吗？普恩特称其为“职责”，更确切地说，是继续担任部长。
“我会面对事情，解释，阐明，”他反驳道。 “我会思考如何改进这个系统，给那些想要乘坐火车旅行并感到平静和安全的人信心。”
民意调查机构益普索 (Ipsos) 的帕科·卡马斯 (Paco Camas) 指出：“这不仅是一次非常严重的事故，而且是短时间内的第二起事故。”

title_en: Lamine Yamal, Raphinha help Barcelona hammer Alaves to retain Liga top spot
title_zh: 拉明·亚马尔、拉菲尼亚帮助巴萨击败阿拉维斯卫冕西甲榜首
summary: Yamal and Raphinha score two goals each as Barcelona recover from last week's loss in El Clasico to move back on top.
summary_zh: 亚马尔和拉菲尼亚各进两球，帮助巴塞罗那从上周国家德比的失利中恢复过来，重新登上榜首。
body_en: Lamine Yamal, Raphinha help Barcelona hammer Alaves to retain Liga top spot | Football | Al Jazeera

Raphinha and Lamine Yamal have each struck twice as Barcelona have thrashed Alaves 6-1 to reclaim their La Liga lead and get back on track after two damaging defeats in the past week.
Earlier, Atletico Madrid, in second, earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante, but Barca moved two points clear of the Rojiblancos by routing the Basque visitors at Camp Nou on Saturday.

Still stinging after a Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain and then last weekend’s La Liga home El Clasico loss against rivals Real Madrid, Hansi Flick’s side found their groove once more on Saturday.
Raphinha netted twice in the first half on either side of a Fermin Lopez strike, and Yamal found the net just before the interval.
The teenage winger netted again midway through the second half, and substitute Anthony Gordon chipped home Barca’s sixth before Mariano Diaz pulled one back for Alaves.
“It was a hard week for us. There was no better place than Camp Nou in front of our fans [to bounce back],” Lopez told Movistar.
“They make the difference, Lamine and Raphinha. With them, we will achieve big things.”
There was a minute of silence at the start of each of the day’s matches in memory of the 69 people killed on Wednesday in a train crash in the province of Toledo.
Barcelona host Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday and travel to face Atletico next Sunday in a table-topping La Liga clash.
Alaves have now gone seven matches without a win but are 10th.
“We have to turn the page quickly,” midfielder Ander Guevara said. “We don’t need to sound the alarms. We know we’re on a bad run, but we’re a mature and humble team.”
Earlier in Valencia, Diego Simeone’s Atletico had temporarily climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants with goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone against Levante.
Atletico recorded a seventh consecutive league win to continue their strong form and put pressure on the reigning champions.
“I’m very happy with the team’s work,” coach Simeone told Movistar.

Lewis Hamilton has taken his first pole position for Ferrari at the Mexico City Grand Prix with Mercedes’s Kimi Antonelli fourth on the grid for a ground-breaking race likely to make the 20-year-old Formula One’s youngest champion.

Antonelli needs only a ninth-place finish at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Sunday to become Italy’s first champion since 1953. He was fifth fastest in qualifying, admitting he felt tense, but will move up a place due to Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, in fourth, taking a grid drop.

The pole, in a time of one minute 16.514 seconds, was a record-extending 105th of Hamilton’s stellar career. While he has had two sprint poles since he joined Ferrari last year, he has not had one at a regular grand prix since Hungary in July 2023 when he was at Mercedes – a wait of 1,197 days.
“Thank you so much. It has been such a long time coming,” Hamilton said over the team radio on Saturday. “Mega job, guys. I am so grateful for the hard work you guys put in.”
Hamilton becomes oldest pole-sitter since 1982
The pole also made the seven-time world champion at the age of 41 the oldest pole-sitter since American Mario Andretti, at 42, at Monza in Italy in 1982.
Germany’s Michael Schumacher, who retired from Mercedes in 2012 and won five titles with Ferrari from 2000 to 2004, had his first pole for Ferrari at the 1996 San Marino Grand Prix.

“It feels great to be able to reward them with a pole, and to have your first Ferrari pole, I mean, it just takes me back to watching Michael get all those pole positions when he was at Ferrari and all those wins. So it’s very, very special,” Hamilton said.

Mercedes’s George Russell, Antonelli’s closest rival but 123 points behind his teammate with only 100 to be won after this weekend, was second fastest – just 0.009 adrift after taking provisional pole only for Hamilton to beat his time. Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc was third and 0.119 off the pace.
Both Hamilton and Russell would have to win if either of the remaining contenders is to keep Antonelli waiting another week for the inevitable.
“I struggled to get a good feeling from the tyres in Q3. I just didn’t have the most confidence. I was a bit tense, I am not going to lie,” the Italian said. “It was a poor lap, too many mistakes.
“It has not been the easiest weekend. There is talk of what is there, and I am not as relaxed.”
McLaren’s Lando Norris, the reigning champion and last year’s winner in Mexico, qualified sixth with Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar seventh.
Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson qualified eighth fastest but had a one-place grid drop for a clash with Verstappen in Friday’s practice.

The New Zealander was then disqualified from the session for a technical breach and sent to the back of the grid. Teammate Arvid Lindblad will start eighth, Alpine’s Pierre Gasly ninth and Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg 10th.

刘易斯·汉密尔顿 (Lewis Hamilton) 在墨西哥城大奖赛上首次为法拉利车队夺得杆位，而梅赛德斯车队的基米·安东内利 (Kimi Antonelli) 则位列第四，这场开创性的比赛很可能让这位 20 岁的车手成为一级方程式赛车最年轻的冠军。
安东内利只需周日在罗德里格斯赛道上获得第九名，就可以成为意大利自 1953 年以来的第一位冠军。他在排位赛中排名第五，承认自己感到紧张，但由于红牛车队的马克斯·维斯塔潘（排名第四）的退赛，他的排名将上升。

汉密尔顿以 1 分 16.514 秒的成绩夺得杆位，这是汉密尔顿职业生涯中第 105 次刷新杆位纪录。虽然自去年加入法拉利以来，他已经获得了两次冲刺杆，但自 2023 年 7 月在匈牙利效力梅赛德斯以来，他在常规大奖赛上还没有获得过一次杆位——等待了 1,197 天。
“非常感谢。这已经等了很长时间了，”汉密尔顿周六在车队广播中说道。 “伙计们，这是一项伟大的工作。我非常感谢你们付出的辛勤工作。”
汉密尔顿成为自1982年以来最年长的杆位得主
这位41岁的七届世界冠军也成为自1982年意大利蒙扎42岁的美国人马里奥·安德雷蒂(Mario Andretti)以来最年长的杆位获得者。
德国车手迈克尔·舒马赫 (Michael Schumacher) 于 2012 年从梅赛德斯退役，并在 2000 年至 2004 年期间随法拉利赢得了五次冠军，并在 1996 年圣马力诺大奖赛上为法拉利赢得了首个杆位。
“能够用杆位奖励他们，并获得你的第一个法拉利杆位，感觉很棒，我的意思是，这让我回想起迈克尔在法拉利时获得所有这些杆位和所有这些胜利。所以这非常非常特别，”汉密尔顿说。
梅赛德斯车队的乔治·拉塞尔是安东内利最接近的对手，但落后他的队友 123 分，而本周末后只剩下 100 分，他位居第二，仅落后 0.009 分，仅落后汉密尔顿取得临时杆位，最终击败了自己的时间。法拉利车队的查尔斯·勒克莱尔 (Charles Leclerc) 落后 0.119 秒，排名第三。
如果剩下的任何一个竞争者想让安东内利再等一周，等待不可避免的比赛，汉密尔顿和拉塞尔都必须获胜。
“第三季度我很难从轮胎中获得良好的感觉。我只是没有最大的信心。我有点紧张，我不会撒谎，”意大利人说。 “这是一圈糟糕的一圈，失误太多。
“这不是最轻松的周末。人们谈论那里发生的事情，但我并不那么放松。”
卫冕冠军、去年墨西哥站冠军迈凯伦车队的兰多·诺里斯在排位赛中获得第六名，红牛车队的伊萨克·哈贾尔则获得第七名。
公牛队的利亚姆·劳森（Liam Lawson）在排位赛中排名第八，但在周五的练习赛中与维斯塔潘发生冲突，排名下降一位。
随后，这位新西兰选手因技术违规被取消了比赛资格，并被安排到了最后发车位。队友阿维德·林德布拉德 (Arvid Lindblad) 将从第八位发车，阿尔派 (Alpine) 的皮埃尔·加斯利 (Pierre Gasly) 第九位，奥迪 (Audi) 的尼科·霍肯伯格 (Nico Hulkenberg) 第十位。

US Midterms 2026: The country is about to get a new Congress. What do voters want? | This Is America

With two days to the United States midterm elections , Democratic and Republican leaders are making last-ditch efforts to woo voters, with the cost-of-living crisis, exacerbated by the US-Israel war on Iran, becoming one of the key talking points.
According to the latest survey, Democrats are still ahead of the Republicans, but several closely fought Senate races may decide which party ends up in control of the US Congress .

On Sunday, President Donald Trump will be campaigning in Iowa and Kansas , while Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic candidate who has faced an increased wave of Islamophobic attacks, will be holding events in Michigan.
Democrats continue to lead Republicans by 51.5 percent to 43.1 percent, according to the latest RealClearPolling average.

A national THP/MM survey conducted on October 28 and 29 put Democrats ahead by 54 percent to 41 percent, while an Emerson College poll conducted from October 24 to 26 showed a 10-point Democratic lead.
Natalie Jackson, a political analyst and pollster, told Al Jazeera that the results reflected public dissatisfaction with Trump and the economy .

“Polling shows an environment that is pretty favourable to the Democrats. The president is very unpopular, Americans feel the pinch of high costs, which are partly due to tariffs and the war in Iran, and the general sentiment is that Republicans did not deliver in the last two years.”
In Kansas, a Washington Post-Schar School poll released on Friday suggested Democrat Adam Hamilton was leading against Republican Senator Roger Marshall by 52 percent to 43 percent.
But another Emerson College survey indicated a tighter race, with Hamilton ahead of Marshall by 50 percent to 47percent.
Doug Heye, a Republican strategist and former communications director for the Republican National Committee, questioned the nine-point lead of the Washington Post-Schar School survey.
“I don’t know how it plays out, but, you know, we saw an outlier poll in Iowa just two years ago that caused a lot of damage to the whole polling industry,” Heye said.

He was referring to a Des Moines Register poll published days before the 2024 presidential election that showed Kamala Harris leading Trump by three percentage points in Iowa. Trump went on to win the state by about 13 points, a difference of 16 points from the poll’s margin.
“A lot of Republicans just don’t want to answer calls from pollsters,” he added.
Jackson, the political analyst, also said polling might not accurately reflect the result of individual Senate contests.
“In some individual races – particularly the close Senate races – we could see polling error that shifts the race in one direction or another,” she said.

2026 年美国中期选举：该国即将迎来新一届国会。选民想要什么？ |这就是美国
距离美国中期选举还有两天，民主党和共和党领导人正在竭尽全力吸引选民，美以对伊朗战争加剧的生活成本危机成为关键话题之一。
根据最新调查，民主党仍领先于共和党，但几场激烈的参议院竞选可能会决定哪个党派最终控制美国国会。

周日，唐纳德·特朗普总统将在爱荷华州和堪萨斯州进行竞选活动，而面临越来越多的伊斯兰恐惧症攻击的民主党候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德将在密歇根州举行活动。
根据最新的 RealClearPolling 平均值，民主党继续以 51.5% 对 43.1% 领先共和党。
10月28日至29日进行的全国THP/MM调查显示民主党领先54%至41%，而艾默生学院10月24日至26日进行的民意调查显示民主党领先10个百分点。
政治分析师兼民意调查专家娜塔莉·杰克逊告诉半岛电视台，结果反映了公众对特朗普和经济的不满。
“民意调查显示，环境对民主党相当有利。总统非常不受欢迎，美国人感到高成本的压力，部分原因是关税和伊朗战争，普遍的情绪是共和党在过去两年没有兑现承诺。”
在堪萨斯州，华盛顿邮报夏尔学校周五公布的一项民意调查显示，民主党人亚当·汉密尔顿以 52% 比 43% 领先共和党参议员罗杰·马歇尔。
但艾默生学院的另一项调查显示，竞争更加激烈，汉密尔顿以 50% 比 47% 领先马歇尔。
共和党战略家、共和党全国委员会前通讯主任道格·海耶对华盛顿邮报沙尔学院调查的九个百分点的领先优势提出质疑。
海耶说：“我不知道结果如何，但是，你知道，两年前我们在爱荷华州看到了一次异常民意调查，对整个民意调查行业造成了很大损害。”
他指的是 2024 年总统大选前几天发布的《得梅因纪事报》民意调查，该民意调查显示卡马拉·哈里斯在爱荷华州领先特朗普三个百分点。特朗普随后以约 13 个百分点的优势赢得该州，与民意调查的差距相差 16 个百分点。
“很多共和党人只是不想回应民意调查人员的电话，”他补充道。
政治分析家杰克逊还表示，民意调查可能无法准确反映个别参议院竞选的结果。
她说：“在一些个人竞选中，尤其是势均力敌的参议院竞选中，我们可能会看到民意调查错误，导致竞选朝着一个方向或另一个方向转变。”
